request.spec:
A claim can be shared with other people on the sheet: a person select, a share percent (two
decimals, more than 0.00) and a button on the claim (CLAIM_SHARED naming the claim, ending
with=<person> share=<share>; the claim's own person, a person already holding a share, or shares
totalling more than 100.00 are refused; a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim cannot be shared). Each
holder's due-total includes their part: the claim's due times their share divided by 100, rounded
half to even; the claim's own person's due-total counts the claim's due less the holders' parts,
and each person's settled-total and open-total count the same part. Show the holders on the claim as
<name> <share>, comma and space separated.
request.prompt:

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A claim can be shared with other people on the sheet: a person select, a share percent (two
decimals, more than 0.00) and a button on the claim (CLAIM_SHARED naming the claim, ending
with=<person> share=<share>; the claim's own person, a person already holding a share, or shares
totalling more than 100.00 are refused; a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim cannot be shared). Each
holder's due-total includes their part: the claim's due times their share divided by 100, rounded
half to even; the claim's own person's due-total counts the claim's due less the holders' parts,
and each person's settled-total and open-total count the same part. Show the holders on the claim as

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Claims can now be shared, and the full `bin/e2e` run passes all 4 tests (the main "shared claims" test and scenarios 1–3).

**What a user sees on each claim**
- A "Share with" person select, a share-percent field and a Share button.
- The holders, shown as `Ben 33.33, Cam 33.33`.
- A refused share shows the claim's error and writes nothing. That covers: the claim's own person, a person who already holds a share, a percent of 0.00 or less, shares totalling more than 100.00, and a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim.
- A successful share writes `CLAIM_SHARED … with=<name> share=<pct>` to the audit file, followed by the usual ROLLUP/TOTALS lines.

**How the totals work**
- Each holder's part is the claim's due × their share / 100, rounded half to even.
- The claim's own person counts the due less all the holders' parts.
- Holders' parts count in their due-total, settled-total and open-total. A part also stops a holder's due-total from showing n/a when their own grade has no rate (Cam in the test).
- This is done on the server (`Rollup.java`, which produces the audit's ROLLUP/TOTALS lines) and on the screen (`rates.ts`). I also passed the parts to every other place that shows a person's due-total (header, classic, summary, crews, consolidated, sort, export, tree search, snapshot compare) so they agree.
- Shares are stored in a new `claim_share` table (migration `V118__claim_share.sql`), and the endpoint is `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/share`.

**A fix outside the feature itself.** Scenario 3 failed every time at a settle-part step that had nothing to do with sharing. When a second user opened the sheet, the sheet id appeared before the person rows. The rows stay hidden until the user's role has loaded, and the sheet loader didn't wait for it. The test's helper then treated an existing claim as newly created. The loader (`SheetLoader.tsx`) now also loads the role and crews before showing the sheet as active, which is what its own comment already said it did.

**Left as is:**
- Overdue-totals and the person score still count a shared claim's full figure for its own person, since the request only named the due, settled and open totals.
- Statement and period due-totals don't include shares.
- When the sheet is viewed as of an earlier date, it shows today's shares, because shares aren't dated.
- `statement.slot.tsx` already had TypeScript errors (undefined `queryClient`, `sheetId`, `person`) before my change. The build doesn't type-check, so it still builds, and I didn't touch it.

While debugging I found something else is already serving on port 3000 on this machine. This shell has `PORT=3001`, so `bin/e2e` runs on 3001.
